steps.title: Turn on the kit ruff rules for alpha
steps.why: ruff selects only E, F, I, UP and B; the kit also bans catch-all excepts (BLE), commented-out code (ERA), blanket or stale suppressions (PGH, RUF100), late imports (PLC0415) and raising bare Exception (TRY002).

steps.title: Make pyright strict for tests and stale ignores
steps.why: tests/ is checked in standard mode and an unneeded type: ignore goes unnoticed; the kit checks everything strictly and reports unnecessary ignores.

steps.title: Add deptry as the structure check of alpha
steps.why: Nothing checks for unused, missing or transitive dependencies; the kit runs deptry as the structure step.

steps.title: Block every way to skip the commit hooks
steps.why: guard_bash matches only the exact --no-verify, so an abbreviated --no-verif, core.hooksPath set through GIT_CONFIG_* or git --config-env all commit past a failing commit-msg hook; this breaks R3.

acceptance.run: uv run pytest -k "abbreviated_no_verify or env_hooks_path or config_env"

steps.title: Keep license_file relative to the project
steps.why: The identity skill says to save an absolute license_file path, which commits a machine path into project.json and breaks load_answers on every other clone.

steps.title: Bound toolchain and check commands in time
steps.why: About 30 of 45 subprocess calls (uv sync, pnpm install, mise install, cargo, a legacy test suite) have no timeout and capture output, so a prompt or a stalled download looks like a silent freeze; two comments justifying this are wrong.

steps.title: Parse principles.toml into typed data
steps.why: load_project_principles returns raw TOML that 23 functions index as dict[str, Any]; a hand edit gives a traceback, and a blanket except KeyError names the wrong cause.

steps.title: Report an unreadable project.json
steps.why: project_book swallows invalid JSON and bootstrap then says No recipe for stack; refresh_manifest returns silently, so file hashes go stale.

steps.title: Write project.json atomically everywhere
steps.why: write_answers replaces project.json atomically, but write_json, used by generate, refresh_manifest, apply_update and adopt, writes in place, so an interrupted write can lose the answers.

steps.title: Keep one git status parser
steps.why: adopt and update each parse git status --porcelain -z; adopt ignores the exit code, so a failed git status reads as a clean tree and apply can write over files. The default-branch lookup is also written three times.

steps.title: Give every suppression a reason or a fix
steps.why: src/ and project-files/ hold 17 type or pyright ignores and 15 noqa E402 comments with no reason or decision, which the kit blocks in generated projects.

acceptance.run: ! grep -rnE "# (type: ignore|pyright: ignore|noqa)(\[[^]]*\]|: [A-Z0-9, ]+)?[[:space:]]*$" src project-files/hooks project-files/checks

steps.title: Stop the shortcuts check reading string literals
steps.why: The shortcuts check matches # shortcut: anywhere on a line, so test fixtures that hold one in a string fail it; tests/checks/test_shortcuts.py now splits its fixtures to avoid that.

steps.title: Allowlist folders that nested gitignores skip
steps.why: The generated .betterleaks.toml lists only the root .gitignore, so a folder ignored by its own .gitignore (here .superpowers/) is scanned; it was added to the allowlist by hand.

steps.title: Drop CI wording when CI is none
steps.why: With build.ci none, the generated CLAUDE.md still says CI runs the same checks, and mise.toml says ci runs what CI runs on a pull request.

steps.title: Sort alpha tests into unit, integration, e2e
steps.why: Tests sit flat in tests/ with slow ones marked by name; the testing answer puts each level under tests/<level>/.

acceptance.run: test -d tests/unit && test -d tests/integration && test -d tests/end-to-end && ! ls tests/test_*.py

steps.title: Test the 200 ms startup budget
steps.why: The performance answer holds bin/alpha to startup under 200 ms, measured by a timing test that does not exist yet.

steps.title: Publish the missing GitHub releases
steps.why: The changelog is GitHub releases, but v0.2.0, v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 are tagged with no release notes.

acceptance.run: gh release view v0.2.0 -R vs/alpha && gh release view v0.4.1 -R vs/alpha && gh release view v0.4.2 -R vs/alpha

steps.title: Link R1-R7 to the tests that cover them
steps.why: Few tests name a requirement id, so the acceptance checks of R1-R7 do not trace to tests.

acceptance.run: for r in R1 R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 R7; do grep -rqw $r tests || exit 1; done

steps.title: Measure coverage of alpha's changed lines
steps.why: Pull requests must cover 80% of the lines they change, but alpha's recipe has no coverage command.

overrides.reason: mise run check runs locally before each commit, and the slow tests and evals need real toolchains and paid tokens that CI should not spend.

decisions.title: Product identity
decisions.context: alpha is an existing Claude Code plugin being adopted; its README states what it does. It serves developers who want agents held to engineering principles in new and existing repos.
decisions.decision: Name alpha (slug alpha), for developers building with Claude Code; requirements R1 (interview), R2 (generate), R3 (enforce), R4 (adopt), R5 (extend), R6 (recipes), R7 (user layer). MIT, keeping the repo LICENSE; domain jargon on.
decisions.consequences: Features outside R1-R7 need a new requirement first. The glossary and One vocabulary principle apply to code, docs and skills.

decisions.title: Single Python CLI
decisions.context: alpha is one Python package (src/alpha, src/alpha_evals) driven through bin/alpha and the plugin skills; the survey found one candidate at the root.
decisions.decision: One component, alpha: kind cli, stack alpha-python (adopted, extends the kit python recipe), path . (single layout). Traits: network calls (subprocesses), persisted data (project.json, user layer, baselines), non-trivial logic; no UI, not deployed, no ML.
decisions.consequences: One toolchain to maintain (uv, Python 3.11+). Subprocess calls need timeouts and failure paths; project.json and the user layer need a migration path on schema change. The recipe runs the commands mise.toml already runs; deptry and coverage are not set up yet.

decisions.title: One component, no contracts
decisions.context: alpha is a single component; nothing calls another component, but the domain has its own vocabulary.
decisions.decision: alpha turns interview answers into an enforced project (generate, adopt, update) and checks the answers, recipes, baselines and adoption steps that drive it. No calls, contract format none. Glossary: kit, area, component, recipe, principle, override, baseline, adoption step.
decisions.consequences: These eight terms are fixed names across code, docs and skills; a new concept needs a glossary entry. Splitting off a component would need contracts.

decisions.title: Messages and exit codes
decisions.context: alpha errors reach a developer at the terminal or Claude running a skill, which relays the fix.
decisions.decision: alpha uses message-and-exit-code: alpha: <problem> and its fix on stderr, non-zero exit. Categories: validation, not-found, conflict, unavailable, internal (the kit defaults).
decisions.consequences: Every error names what went wrong and the next step to fix it, so a skill can act on it without guessing.

decisions.title: Unit, integration and end-to-end tests
decisions.context: The risk is in subprocess calls, file merges and stored state, and in whole flows (interview, generate, adopt, update) users drive through bin/alpha and the skills.
decisions.decision: alpha: unit, integration (the real-toolchain tests now marked slow) and end-to-end (whole flows from R1-R7). Diff coverage 80% (kit default).
decisions.consequences: A test covering an acceptance check names its requirement id (R1-R7). Today tests are flat under tests/ and few name a requirement; moving them under tests/<level>/ and linking them is part of the adoption plan. Diff coverage applies once the recipe has a coverage command.

decisions.title: No UI
decisions.context: alpha runs in a terminal and inside Claude Code; no component shows a user interface.
decisions.decision: No UI components.
decisions.consequences: The visual-system and accessibility principles do not apply; adding a UI component reopens this area.

decisions.title: README as user docs
decisions.context: Users meet alpha through the README and three skills; developers through CLAUDE.md. The kit usual CLI globs match nothing here.
decisions.decision: User docs live in README.md (kit default). Mapped: src/alpha/cli.py and bin/** to README.md or CLAUDE.md; skills/new-project, skills/adopt and skills/extend to README.md. Decision records start at 0001 in docs/decisions/.
decisions.consequences: A change to the CLI or a user-invoked skill must update the README (or CLAUDE.md for the CLI), or the Stop hook blocks it.

decisions.title: No CI, plugin package
decisions.context: alpha is published as a Claude Code plugin through its own marketplace on GitHub (vs/alpha); nothing is deployed. The kit default is GitHub Actions.
decisions.decision: CI: none (loosens build-hosting-upfront). No environments. alpha builds into a package (the plugin, published through its marketplace); no hosting.
decisions.consequences: Nothing checks a push remotely: mise run check (and the commit hooks) are the only gate, so run them before every commit. Not made a default for future projects.

decisions.title: Local CLI, no secrets or auth
decisions.context: alpha runs on the user machine and is not deployed; the evals use the claude CLI login, which alpha never handles.
decisions.decision: No secret store (nothing deployed; local .env files suffice). Auth: none. No extra protected paths.
decisions.consequences: Claude cannot edit .env files, keys or lockfiles (always protected); the betterleaks check blocks a committed secret. Baseline-output fixtures stay editable so they can be re-recorded.

decisions.title: Weekly manual updates
decisions.context: One toolchain (uv) plus the mise-pinned check tools drift. The kit default is Dependabot, but with no CI nothing would check its pull requests.
decisions.decision: Updates: manual (kit default dependabot), weekly, after a 7-day cooldown from each release.
decisions.consequences: Someone runs the updates weekly with uv and mise, and checks them locally with mise run check before committing; a new dependency still needs its row in docs/dependencies.md. Not made a default for future projects.

decisions.title: Nothing deployed
decisions.context: alpha runs only on the user machine; no component is deployed.
decisions.decision: No observability setup.
decisions.consequences: Observability applies once a component is deployed; that reopens this area.

decisions.title: Semver tags with GitHub releases
decisions.context: Plugin users update through the marketplace and read release notes on GitHub. The repo already tags vX.Y.Z on main and has GitHub releases, but no CHANGELOG.md; the kit default changelog is a file.
decisions.decision: Scheme semver, changelog github-releases (kit default file), scope repo. Process: a chore: Release X.Y.Z commit bumps plugin.json, pyproject.toml, src/alpha/__init__.py and uv.lock; tag vX.Y.Z on main and publish a GitHub release with its notes.
decisions.consequences: A breaking change to answers, recipes or the CLI is a major version (minor while 0.x) and its release notes say how to migrate. v0.2.0, v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 have tags but no GitHub release yet. Not made a default for future projects.

decisions.title: Versioned JSON and TOML files
decisions.context: alpha stores answers in each project (project.json, schema 1), the user layer in ~/.config/alpha/ and baseline files; they outlive the plugin version that wrote them.
decisions.decision: Storage: JSON and TOML files. Migration tool: none today; answers refuses any schema but 1, and skills treat a missing area as pending. No ML.
decisions.consequences: Bumping project.json schema needs an upgrader that rewrites older files, with tests, before release; until then a shape change must stay backward compatible. There are no migration files, so the append-only rule has nothing to guard.

decisions.title: No accessibility target
decisions.context: alpha has no user interface beyond the terminal and Claude Code.
decisions.decision: No accessibility target or checks.
decisions.consequences: The accessibility principle does not apply; adding a UI component reopens this area.

decisions.title: CLI startup budget
decisions.context: Skills call bin/alpha many times per interview and hook, so a slow start adds up; the load is one developer on a laptop.
decisions.decision: alpha: startup < 200 ms (kit default for a CLI), measured by an end-to-end pytest test timing bin/alpha --help, run by mise run check. Today it starts in about 60-70 ms.
decisions.consequences: Breaking the budget needs a fix or a decision record. The timing test does not exist yet; it is an adoption step.

decisions.title: Conventional commits on feature branches
decisions.context: One maintainer and Claude commit; 48 of the last 50 commits already follow conventional commits (the other two are merges), with scopes hooks, recipes, defaults and spec in use.
decisions.decision: Convention: conventional. Scopes: alpha, hooks, recipes, defaults, spec. Branching: feature-branches merged into main. Git hooks: alpha sets core.hooksPath (no hook manager found).
decisions.consequences: The commit-msg hook rejects a header that is not type(scope): description with a 50-char imperative description, or body lines past 72; merge, revert and fixup commits pass. Existing history stays as it is.

decisions.title: Review at merge
decisions.context: Work happens on feature branches verified once when finished; a review per task would slow small changes, and the hooks already check every edit.
decisions.decision: Review mode at-merge (kit default); max_lines 200 and max_files 5 recorded for batched mode; no extra risk paths beyond the kit ones.
decisions.consequences: Claude stops for the principles reviewer before pushing to main or merging a pull request, and cannot finish with open findings.

identity.name: alpha
identity.value_proposition: alpha interviews you about a new project, then writes what agents build on: principles, docs, decision records, Claude Code and git hooks, CI, and a test setup per component that passes from the first commit. It writes no app code, and each principle is checked, by a hook or by a reviewer agent, before a change reaches main.
identity.target_users: Developers building with Claude Code who want agents to follow enforced engineering principles from day one: starting a new project from an enforced skeleton, or bringing an existing repo under the same rules without stopping its work.

requirements.text: Interview the user area by area, recommending answers from the kit defaults, and save them to project.json.
requirements.acceptance: Given an empty folder, when /alpha:new-project runs and the user accepts each recommendation, then project.json has every area done and alpha answers check prints ok.

requirements.text: From finished answers, generate, bootstrap and commit a skeleton (config, docs, test wiring, enforcement, no app code) whose checks pass.
requirements.acceptance: Given finished answers, when alpha generate, bootstrap and commit-skeleton run, then the project has no app source files, every component check and mise run ci pass, and the tree is clean.

requirements.text: Enforce each active principle in a generated project through Claude Code hooks, git hooks, CI or the principles reviewer.
requirements.acceptance: Given a generated project, when an agent skips git hooks, edits a protected file or stops with untested source, then the matching hook blocks it with a message naming the fix.

requirements.text: Bring an existing repo under the same enforcement on alpha/adopt, with legacy findings baselined and a compliance plan to work through.
requirements.acceptance: Given a clean repo with legacy lint findings, when alpha adopt apply and bootstrap --capture-baselines run, then the files alpha writes are committed on alpha/adopt, the existing findings pass as baselined, and a new finding fails its check.

requirements.text: Change the answers of a generated or adopted project and merge the result without overwriting edits the user made.
requirements.acceptance: Given a generated project with a hand edit in CLAUDE.md, when an answer changes and alpha update and commit-update run, then the change is applied, the edit survives, and a second update --dry-run prints nothing to change.

requirements.text: Support any stack through recipes: the ones the kit ships (Python, TypeScript, Rust) or drafted ones that must be proven before use.
requirements.acceptance: Given a stack the kit has no recipe for, when a drafted recipe is saved, then answers check refuses it until alpha recipe try proves it, and again after any later edit.

requirements.text: Apply the user layer (their own defaults and recipes) on top of the kit, surviving plugin updates.
requirements.acceptance: Given a user override set with alpha defaults set, when the plugin is updated or a new interview starts, then alpha defaults show returns the override on top of the kit defaults.

commands.lint: uv run ruff check src tests project-files
commands.format: uv run ruff format src tests project-files
commands.format_check: uv run ruff format --check src tests project-files

glossary.meaning: The defaults, recipes, registry and templates alpha ships, which every project starts from.
One topic of the interview (identity, components, ...), settled by its own skill and saved in project.json.
One part of a project with its own folder, kind, stack and checks; also a commit scope.
How a component on a stack is set up and checked: the kit's own, one drafted for a project, or one adopted from a repo's tools; proven before use.
A rule in docs/principles.toml, enforced by a hook, a check or the principles reviewer.
A project's recorded change to a principle (tighten, loosen or drop), with its reason.
The legacy findings of one check in an adopted repo, per file and rule; only new findings fail and it only shrinks.
One item of an adopted repo's compliance plan, done only when its acceptance conditions hold.

decisions.context: One maintainer and Claude commit; 48 of the last 50 commits already follow conventional commits (the other two are merges), with scopes hooks, recipes, defaults and spec in use.
decisions.decision: Convention: conventional. Scopes: alpha, hooks, recipes, defaults, spec. Branching: feature-branches merged into main. Git hooks: alpha sets core.hooksPath (no hook manager found).
decisions.consequences: The commit-msg hook rejects a header that is not type(scope): description with a 50-char imperative description, or body lines past 72; merge, revert and fixup commits pass. Existing history stays as it is.

decisions.title: Review at merge
decisions.context: Work happens on feature branches verified once when finished; a review per task would slow small changes, and the hooks already check every edit.
decisions.decision: Review mode at-merge (kit default); max_lines 200 and max_files 5 recorded for batched mode; no extra risk paths beyond the kit ones.
decisions.consequences: Claude stops for the principles reviewer before pushing to main or merging a pull request, and cannot finish with open findings.

identity.name: alpha
identity.value_proposition: alpha interviews you about a new project, then writes what agents build on: principles, docs, decision records, Claude Code and git hooks, CI, and a test setup per component that passes from the first commit. It writes no app code, and each principle is checked, by a hook or by a reviewer agent, before a change reaches main.
identity.target_users: Developers building with Claude Code who want agents to follow enforced engineering principles from day one: starting a new project from an enforced skeleton, or bringing an existing repo under the same rules without stopping its work.

requirements.text: Interview the user area by area, recommending answers from the kit defaults, and save them to project.json.
requirements.acceptance: Given an empty folder, when /alpha:new-project runs and the user accepts each recommendation, then project.json has every area done and alpha answers check prints ok.

requirements.text: From finished answers, generate, bootstrap and commit a skeleton (config, docs, test wiring, enforcement, no app code) whose checks pass.
requirements.acceptance: Given finished answers, when alpha generate, bootstrap and commit-skeleton run, then the project has no app source files, every component check and mise run ci pass, and the tree is clean.

requirements.text: Enforce each active principle in a generated project through Claude Code hooks, git hooks, CI or the principles reviewer.
requirements.acceptance: Given a generated project, when an agent skips git hooks, edits a protected file or stops with untested source, then the matching hook blocks it with a message naming the fix.

requirements.text: Bring an existing repo under the same enforcement on alpha/adopt, with legacy findings baselined and a compliance plan to work through.
requirements.acceptance: Given a clean repo with legacy lint findings, when alpha adopt apply and bootstrap --capture-baselines run, then the files alpha writes are committed on alpha/adopt, the existing findings pass as baselined, and a new finding fails its check.

requirements.text: Change the answers of a generated or adopted project and merge the result without overwriting edits the user made.
requirements.acceptance: Given a generated project with a hand edit in CLAUDE.md, when an answer changes and alpha update and commit-update run, then the change is applied, the edit survives, and a second update --dry-run prints nothing to change.

requirements.text: Support any stack through recipes: the ones the kit ships (Python, TypeScript, Rust) or drafted ones that must be proven before use.
requirements.acceptance: Given a stack the kit has no recipe for, when a drafted recipe is saved, then answers check refuses it until alpha recipe try proves it, and again after any later edit.

requirements.text: Apply the user layer (their own defaults and recipes) on top of the kit, surviving plugin updates.
requirements.acceptance: Given a user override set with alpha defaults set, when the plugin is updated or a new interview starts, then alpha defaults show returns the override on top of the kit defaults.

commands.lint: uv run ruff check src tests project-files
commands.format: uv run ruff format src tests project-files
commands.format_check: uv run ruff format --check src tests project-files

components.name: alpha
components.responsibility: Turns interview answers into an enforced project (generate, adopt, update) and checks the answers, recipes, baselines and adoption steps that drive it.

glossary.meaning: The defaults, recipes, registry and templates alpha ships, which every project starts from.
One topic of the interview (identity, components, ...), settled by its own skill and saved in project.json.
One part of a project with its own folder, kind, stack and checks; also a commit scope.
How a component on a stack is set up and checked: the kit's own, one drafted for a project, or one adopted from a repo's tools; proven before use.
A rule in docs/principles.toml, enforced by a hook, a check or the principles reviewer.
A project's recorded change to a principle (tighten, loosen or drop), with its reason.
The legacy findings of one check in an adopted repo, per file and rule; only new findings fail and it only shrinks.
One item of an adopted repo's compliance plan, done only when its acceptance conditions hold.

releases.process: Bump the version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json, pyproject.toml and src/alpha/__init__.py (plus uv.lock) in a chore: Release X.Y.Z commit on main, tag vX.Y.Z and publish a GitHub release with its notes. Users get it with claude plugin marketplace update alpha.

components.name: alpha
components.storage: JSON and TOML files: .claude/alpha/project.json (schema 1) in each project, the user layer in ~/.config/alpha/, and per-check baseline files

performance.expected_load: one developer running alpha on a laptop, against one project at a time

budgets.measured_by: an end-to-end pytest test that times bin/alpha --help, run by mise run check
